comment: Recorded Go behavior the Rust bridge deliberately does not reproduce yet. Every entry pins the exact (path-normalized, $ROOT) error text Rust returns instead: the Rust and Swift replays fail when a case starts matching Go (remove the entry), when it succeeds where Rust must refuse, and when Rust's text is anything other than expected_rust, so an entry cannot outlive its cause or hide a different failure.

cases.approval: approved by the owner 2026-11-01 (ADR 0031, divergence D-SYMLINK)
cases.reason: Go follows the symlink and succeeds; Rust never follows a symlink inside the vault tree: opening, listing and verifying walk the whole vault with O_NOFOLLOW (STORE hardening, crates/symvault-store/src/rooted.rs), so one symlink anywhere refuses the whole operation before any entry is touched.
cases.expected_rust: list entries: vault path is a symlink: $ROOT/vault/entries

side_effects_comment: Side-effect differences the byte-comparing replay cannot express (they are not error texts, so they have no expected_rust). The recorded Go bridge never took a backup, so no fixture case triggers them (the replay pre-marks its seed vaults). Each entry names the tests that pin the Rust behavior; crates/symvault-ffi/tests/backup_dir.rs fails when an entry loses its pin, when a pin names a test that does not exist, or when a test of that file has no entry.

side_effects.approval: decision D1 (maintainer, docs/rust-port/contract-matrix.md DIST-005); mobile bridge application recorded in ADR 0031 (divergence D-BACKUP)
side_effects.reason: Go's pkg/mobilebind wrote the vault in place and kept no copy. Rust takes a verified backup of a vault that carries no .symvault-rust marker before the first mutation (OpenVaultWithPassphrase heal/config rewrite, InitVault over an existing vault, WriteEntryJSON) and then writes the marker into the vault directory.
side_effects.rust_behavior: a Go-faithful tar.gz (pre-rust-<label>-<stamp>.tar.gz) is written to the backup directory, restored into scratch and compared with the live tree; only then is the marker written and the mutation performed; later mutations take no further backup

side_effects.approval: decision D1 (maintainer, docs/rust-port/contract-matrix.md DIST-005); mobile bridge application recorded in ADR 0031 (divergence D-BACKUP)
side_effects.reason: Go has no backup directory concept. When the host sets none and neither $XDG_STATE_HOME nor $HOME/$USERPROFILE exists, Rust cannot take the D1 backup and refuses the first mutation instead of writing without one.
side_effects.rust_behavior: the write fails with `cannot determine the backup directory: set HOME or XDG_STATE_HOME` before any vault byte or marker is written

side_effects.approval: decision D1 (maintainer, docs/rust-port/contract-matrix.md DIST-005); mobile bridge application recorded in ADR 0031 (divergence D-BACKUP)
side_effects.reason: symvault_set_backup_dir is a Rust-only addition to the C ABI (additive; ABI revision stays 1). An empty path clears the host's choice and restores $XDG_STATE_HOME/symvault/backups, then $HOME/.local/state/symvault/backups; a relative path is refused and keeps the previous choice.
side_effects.rust_behavior: symvault_set_backup_dir(dir): absolute dir honoured and taking precedence over the environment; empty restores the environment default; relative dir returns status 1 `backup directory must be an absolute path`

side_effects.approval: decision D1 (maintainer, docs/rust-port/contract-matrix.md DIST-005); mobile bridge application recorded in ADR 0031 (divergence D-BACKUP)
side_effects.reason: The backup holds the same encrypted files as the vault, which already travels with the user's iCloud Drive/device backup. On iOS the host (MobileVaultCore) creates Application Support/symaira-vault-backups (0700), sets isExcludedFromBackup, reads the flag back and only then calls SymvaultFFI.setBackupDir; if any step fails the vault call fails before the core touches the vault. Caches is not used (the system may purge it). A physical-device run is still outstanding (FFI-002).
side_effects.go_behavior: no backup, so nothing to exclude
side_effects.rust_behavior: vault calls in MobileVaultCore point the core at the excluded directory first; an unusable directory fails the call
